description: ESDL is a machine-readable language and associated tooling for describing energy assets and their links. It represents production, consumption, storage, transport and conversion components, including their dynamic behaviour, so modelling and GIS tools can exchange a common system description. Users create an ESDL system for a district or region; outputs are structured energy-system models that downstream tools can read. Geographic coverage and time horizon depend on the modelled system. Apache-2.0 source, class documentation and examples of Python and Java integration are public. A limitation is that an ESDL file encodes assumptions and topology but does not by itself solve dispatch or capacity investment; each downstream simulator needs a compatible mapping. ESDL can connect building, electricity and heating models in multi-vector planning. The related catalogue PyPSA model is a separate optimiser, and a translation would need to be checked before use. No asset inventory or package was downloaded.
